observation.visible_scene: First-person point-of-view from a rider on a mat inside an enclosed water-slide flume (watermark 'Attractions 360°'). The left side is a transparent/semi-transparent tube wall covered in rainbow-colored light refractions (caustics) and faint streaks, through which a dim external structure is visible; the right side is an open water channel with rippling surface. A rider's hand grips a yellow looped handle/rope at the bottom of the frame. Far ahead on the right is a rectangular tunnel portal lit with an orange glow, in which a second rider on a mat can be seen. The camera moves forward along the flume.
visible_changes: The rectangular portal and the distant rider within it drift steadily toward the right edge of the frame and eventually leave view, while the caustic-covered transparent wall occupies an increasing share of the image, consistent with the camera/POV yawing leftward as the rider advances.
The hand and yellow handle shift slightly along the bottom edge (toward the lower-right) and remain present throughout most of the excerpt.
The water surface ripples continuously; faint shapes seen through the transparent wall scroll, and a pale elongated silhouette becomes and stays visible on the left portion of the wall.
The overall framing tilts/rotates so that the diagonal line of the wall-to-ceiling junction moves upward across the top of the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Events before this flume section and after the last frame, including whether the portal leads to a drop or another tube segment.
The identity, distance, and motion of the second rider seen through the portal.
What lies outside the transparent wall (the dim structure and the pale elongated shape are not clearly identifiable).
uncertain_details: Whether the rightward drift of the portal is due to camera yaw, the rider's path curving, or both.
Whether the pale elongated shape on the left wall is a reflection, a design element, or a separate object seen through the wall.
The exact motion of the distant rider (approaching, receding, or static) cannot be determined from the limited view.
The yellow handle's role (mat rope vs. grab handle) is not confirmed.
